title: Choose the visual world
question: The bold end, as you asked. Two re-rolls so far: what has been missing? Write it in Steer and the next hand aims at it, or pick a card.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: a cloud's edge diffracting sunlight into pastel bands
options.thesis: White and slate everywhere; colour lives only in thin pastel bands, and on the keys, where the music is.
materials: a narrow mint, rose and lilac fringe
options.viewport: Laptop: step or song in a wide column, choices beside it, the keyboard full width below, its marks in pastel bands; phone: one column, keyboard at the thumb.
options.risk: Pastels can wash out on a sunny music stand; the played key has to go deep, not stay pastel. The source marks the active band violet; here it is rose, since violet was turned down.

raised.raise: Every place says its literal name, so wayfinding is reading.
Regions never move: navigation swaps what is in them, the keyboard stays put.
The key that sounds is the only warm, deep thing on the screen.
Numbers (bars, tempos, counts) sit in tabular columns at an even density.

options.label: Busytown Cutaway
options.lineage: Richard Scarry's labelled cross-section picture books
options.thesis: A cheerful labelled world: every key, chord and control wears its small printed name.
options.viewport: The keyboard drawn as a labelled cutaway, each chord a small building on the road of the song.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity (the labelled keyboard is already the app's teacher); loses on audience, who are adults at church, not children.
options.risk: Reads as a children's app to adult accompanists.

options.label: Industrial Quotes
options.thesis: Labels in straight quotes, hazard stripes, orange tags.
options.viewport: Crate-stencilled labels on a stockroom grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: streetwear irony is foreign to a church music room.
options.risk: Loud where the task wants calm.
options.kept: Every place says its literal name.

options.label: Sixteen Colours
options.thesis: A locked sixteen-colour set, dithered, on a fixed pixel grid.
options.viewport: Fixed frame, a text window docked low.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pixel nostalgia hurts reading at arm's length.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Orange digits glowing in glass on black steel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dark lab instrument, not a daylit piano.
options.kept: The lit thing is the only warm accent.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white bar fields and dense numbers.
options.viewport: A wall of bars with numbers in the margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no colour for chord tones or scales, strobing.
options.risk: Cold and hard to learn from.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Flowkey, Simply Piano and Skoove ship: white screens, one friendly brand colour, plain keys lit in it.
canonCard.viewport: The layout a learner expects from those three, at their level of craft.
